xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2611: pan close: sync-beads teardown step always fails post-Dolt-cutover — ceremony archives .beads/ before syncing, aborts close-out

plan.title: pan close: sync-beads teardown step always fails post-Dolt-cutover — ceremony archives .beads/ before syncing, aborts close-out
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Every first `pan close <id> --force` on a migrated project fails at teardown:sync-beads and aborts the ceremony. Verified root cause (which corrects the issue body's analysis): the archive step only COPIES .beads/ and is not the cause. The real mechanism is a redirect chain — createWorktree writes the workspace .beads/redirect pointing at the project root (../../.beads), and post-Dolt-cutover the project root .beads is itself a redirect to the state worktree. bd refuses redirect chains, falls back to the project root's RETIRED Dolt store, `bd vc status` there reports no Commit line, and exportBeadsJsonl (src/lib/beads/export.ts:60) refuses. Teardown steps don't abort mid-sequence, so removeWorktree still deletes the worktree; the ceremony then aborts before closing the tracker issue, and a second run succeeds only because the workspace branch of teardown skips.
narratives.Proposal: Two surgical fixes plus tests and docs. (1) syncWorkspaceBeadsImpl (src/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.ts:261-279) resolves resolveCanonicalBeadsHome(workspacePath); when non-null it runs exportBeadsJsonl(dirname(canonicalHome), { beadsDir: canonicalHome }) so bd executes where the Dolt store actually lives; when null it keeps today's exportBeadsJsonl(workspacePath). The step's export/list record-count cross-check keeps running at close time — that is the no-loss guarantee. (2) createWorktree (src/lib/workspace-manager/worktree-ops.ts:111-130) writes the redirect as the absolute canonical beads home when resolvable (one hop, mirroring src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts:437-443), keeping the relative ../../.beads fallback only when resolution returns null. Exact before/after snippets are in the PRD draft (drafts/pan-2611.md on overdeck-state).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Repairing existing workspaces' chained redirect files (live stale-read hazard for running agents — deserves a follow-up issue; close-out no longer depends on workspace-side resolution after item 1)
- Removing the retired project-root Dolt residue (embeddeddolt.retired-cutover-20260712) — operator-owned state
- Retiring the teardown:sync-beads step — it stays as the close-time no-loss validation
- Reordering the close-out ceremony or changing archive-planning — the archive step was exonerated
- Anything in PAN-2613's scope (bd bootstrap re-clone failures inside runMutationBatch)

autoDecisions.summary: Re-route the sync-beads export to the canonical beads home instead of retiring the step or reordering the ceremony.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue offered three options (run against state worktree, run before archive, retire). Reordering fixes nothing — verified that archive only copies .beads/. Retiring loses the close-time record-count validation. Re-routing preserves the no-loss check and fixes the failure; verified live that `bd vc status` at the state worktree reports Commit c7e4uovo while the workspace resolution does not.

autoDecisions.summary: Also fix the redirect writer in worktree-ops.ts so new worktrees get a one-hop redirect to the canonical home.
autoDecisions.rationale: It is the source of the chain and violates the documented contract (docs/BEADS.md:16-18 says worktrees point at the canonical home). src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts:437-443 already writes the canonical path — this aligns the second writer with the first.

autoDecisions.summary: Defer repairing existing workspaces' chained redirects to a follow-up issue.
autoDecisions.rationale: Different blast radius: it affects live agent bd reads (stale data), not close-out, and touching every existing workspace is beyond this issue's fix expectations. Recorded as hazard H3 in continue.json.

items.title: Re-route teardown:sync-beads export to the canonical beads home

narrative.Action: In syncWorkspaceBeadsImpl (src/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.ts:261-279): add `import { resolveCanonicalBeadsHome } from '../beads/home.js';` (dirname is already imported from path on line 3). Keep the existing existsSync(workspaceBeadsDir) skip guard unchanged. Before the try block, compute `const canonicalHome = resolveCanonicalBeadsHome(workspacePath);`. Inside the try, call `exportBeadsJsonl(dirname(canonicalHome), { beadsDir: canonicalHome })` when canonicalHome is non-null, otherwise keep `exportBeadsJsonl(workspacePath)` exactly as today. Success/failure messages unchanged. Exact before/after snippet in PRD WI-1 (drafts/pan-2611.md). Do NOT use execSync or add any new child_process call — exportBeadsJsonl already owns the async bd invocation.

narrative.Action: In createWorktree (src/lib/workspace-manager/worktree-ops.ts:111-130): add `import { resolveCanonicalBeadsHome } from '../beads/home.js';`. Compute `const canonicalHome = resolveCanonicalBeadsHome(targetPath);` and `const sourceBeadsDir = canonicalHome ?? join(repoPath, '.beads');`. Keep the existsSync(sourceBeadsDir) gate, the !existsSync(redirectPath) no-overwrite guard, and the non-fatal try/catch. expected_outputs: teardown-workspace.test.ts passes including the four new sync-beads cases

narrative.Action: Extend tests/unit/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.test.ts (it already vi.mocks child_process, util, tmux, paths, shadow-state). Add vi.mock for '../../../../src/lib/beads/export.js' (exportBeadsJsonl) and '../../../../src/lib/beads/home.js' (resolveCanonicalBeadsHome). Create the workspace under mkdtempSync temp dirs with a real .beads/redirect file so the existsSync guard passes without mocking fs. Drive through the exported teardownWorkspace with deleteWorkspace behavior enabled. Four cases: (1) home resolves to /state/proj/.beads → exportBeadsJsonl called with ('/state/proj', { beadsDir: '/state/proj/.beads' }), step ok; (2) home null → exportBeadsJsonl called with the workspace path and no beadsDir; (3) workspace .beads absent → step skipped, export never called; (4) exportBeadsJsonl rejects → step failed with the error text in the message. No timers are involved — do not add real delays; the fake-timers rule does not apply here.

narrative.Action: Create tests/unit/lib/workspace-manager/worktree-ops.test.ts. Mock child_process/util following the pattern at the top of tests/unit/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.test.ts so createWorktree's execAsync git calls no-op successfully, and vi.mock '../../../../src/lib/beads/home.js'. Three cases: (1) canonical home resolvable and existing → redirect file content equals the absolute canonical path; (2) canonical null + <repoPath>/.beads exists → redirect content equals relative(targetPath, <repoPath>/.beads); (3) pre-existing redirect file → content unchanged after createWorktree. No timers involved — no fake-timers setup needed.

narrative.Action: In docs/BEADS.md, 'Local topology' section (the paragraph around lines 14-19 describing .beads/redirect files): extend it to state that (a) redirects are always one hop — bd refuses redirect chains and falls back to the redirect target's own directory, so a redirect must never point at another redirecting directory; (b) worktree creation writes the canonical home path directly (never the project root, which is itself a redirect post-cutover); (c) the close-out teardown:sync-beads step validates and refreshes the recovery export from the canonical home, not from inside the workspace. Keep the section's existing terse style. No Mintlify configuration/ page documents redirect mechanics (verified during planning), so docs/BEADS.md is the only doc surface touched.
